subject: Agriculture
title: Agroforestry
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Agroforestry.

hook.text: Trees and crops together produce more total food per hectare than either alone. The combination is agroforestry.

buildup.text: Fruit or nut trees are planted in rows with annual crops growing between them. Each uses different light and soil layers.

discovery.text: Tree roots access deep water and nutrients, then cycle them to the surface via leaf litter—helping shallow-rooted crops.

twist.text: Trees take years to produce returns. Farmers need income today. This time lag slows adoption worldwide.

climax.text: Coffee, cacao, and vanilla grown under shade trees produce premium quality while sequestering carbon.

punchline.text: Trees are the patient farmer's best investment. The soil knows it immediately.

quiz.question: Why do agroforestry systems outproduce monocultures per hectare?
options: Trees and crops use different light and soil layers, maximizing total resource capture

details.summary: Agroforestry is the practice of integrating trees with crops or livestock on the same land. This topic covers alley cropping, windbreaks, riparian buffers, and how trees improve farm productivity, biodiversity, and climate resilience.
details.whyItMatters: Agroforestry systems can increase total farm output by 40% or more compared to monocultures. They sequester carbon, prevent erosion, diversify farm income, and create habitat for beneficial wildlife.
takeaways: Agroforestry combines trees with crops or livestock for mutual benefit
Common systems include alley cropping, silvopasture, and riparian buffers
Trees provide shade, windbreaks, nitrogen fixation, and additional income streams

faq.question: What are the main types of agroforestry systems?
faq.answer: Alley cropping grows crops between rows of trees. Silvopasture integrates trees with livestock grazing. Riparian buffers plant trees along waterways to filter runoff. Forest farming cultivates shade-loving crops under a tree canopy.

faq.question: How do trees benefit crop production in agroforestry?
faq.answer: Trees provide windbreaks that reduce crop desiccation, shade that lowers heat stress, leaf litter that adds organic matter, and deep roots that bring up nutrients from lower soil layers. Nitrogen-fixing trees like acacia directly fertilize neighboring crops.
